items.title: Building Material Price Inflation Remains High Despite Energy Price Declines
items.description: Building Material Price Inflation Remains High Despite Energy Price Declines November 13, 2026 Jesse Wade No Comments The Producer Price Index for final demand was up 0.3% in October, after rising 1.4% in September. Compared to a year ago, final demand prices were up 6.5%. The price of goods used in new residential construction (including energy) was unchanged over the month and up 9.8% from last year, while the price of services was up 0.7% over the month and up 11.3% from last year. Combining goods and services, the price index for inputs to new residential construction was up 0.3% in October and 10.4% higher than last year. Input Goods The goods component has a larger importance to the inputs to residential construction price index, representing around 60% of the total. On a monthly basis, the price of input goods to new residential construction was unchanged in October after rising 1.7% in September. The input goods to residential construction index can be further broken down into two separate components, one measuring energy inputs with the other measuring remaining goods. The latter of these two components simply represents building materials used in residential construction, which makes up around 93% of the goods index. Energy input prices fell 3.3% in October and were 64.8% higher than a year ago. Building material prices were up 0.5% in October and up 5.8% compared to one year ago. Energy prices fell monthly as No. 2 diesel fuel prices fell 4.6% over the month but was a substantial 115.2% higher than a year ago. Outside of energy products, particleboard and fiberboard prices rose 5.4% over the month and were up 13.9% from a year ago. Softwood veneer and plywood prices were up 3.6% over the month and 24.5% higher than a year ago. Input Services Prices for service inputs to residential construction rose 0.7% in October. On a year-over-year basis, service input prices were up 11.3%. The price index for service inputs to residential construction can be broken out into three separate components: a trade services component, a transportation and warehousing services component, and a services excluding trade, transportation, and warehousing component (other services). The most significant component is trade services (around 60%), followed by other services (around 29%), and finally transportation and warehousing services (around 11%). The largest component, trade services, was up 13.2% from a year ago. The price of transportation and warehousing services has risen 24.6% from a year ago, while prices for other services were up 3.0% over the year. items.description: NMHC and RETTC say Democrats have won both chambers, producing divided government, and argue housing costs are the issue candidates in both parties campaigned on. About 20% of the 120th Congress will be new, which the groups see as a chance to educate lawmakers on supply, permitting and technology that can cut costs. The apartment industry wants Congress to build on the ROAD to Housing Act and favors a balanced approach to affordability measures that avoids driving up costs. items.title: No Relief: Credit Conditions for Builders Still Tightening
items.description: No Relief: Credit Conditions for Builders Still Tightening November 13, 2026 Paul Emrath No Comments Credit conditions on loans for residential Land Acquisition, Development & Construction (AD&C) were still tightening in the third quarter of 2026, according to NAHB’s quarterly survey on AD&C Financing. The net easing index derived from the survey posted a third-quarter reading of -15.3 (the negative number indicating net tightening). This marks the nineteenth consecutive quarter during which residential builders and developers have reported tightening credit conditions. The NAHB survey agrees closely with the third-quarter results reported by lenders in the Federal Reserve’s survey of senior loan officers, as the net easing index constructed from the Fed survey posted a third-quarter reading of -15.5. Although lenders previously reported a slight easing in 2026 Q2, lenders have generally agreed with builders and developers that credit conditions have been tightening since the beginning of 2022. The Fed survey’s net easing index was in negative territory (indicating net tightening) for 18 of the past 19 quarters. More details from the Fed’s survey of lenders—including measures of demand and net easing for residential mortgages—appeared in a previous post . Meanwhile, measures on the cost of AD&C credit exhibited a combination of relatively small quarter-to-quarter changes, signaling no clear trend in either direction. The average contract interest rate declined from 8.09% in the second quarter to 7.83% in the third quarter on loans for land development, but increased for the other three categories of loans tracked in the NAHB AD&C survey: from 7.77% to 8.08% on loans for land acquisition, from 7.28% to 7.72% on loans for speculative single-family construction, and from 7.01% to 7.27% on loans for pre-sold single-family construction. However, the initial points charged by lenders declined on all four categories of AD&C loans in the third quarter: from 1.05% to 0.86% on loans for land acquisition, from 1.05% to 0.97% on loans for land development, from 0.85% to 0.71% on loans for speculative single-family construction, and from 0.71% to 0.51% on loans for pre-sold single-family construction. Those changes left the average effective interest rate (taking both contract rate and initial points into account) essentially unchanged at 11.83% (compared 11.82% in the second quarter) on loans for speculative single-family construction. The average effective rate increased from 10.43% to 10.55% on loans for land acquisition, but declined from 12.59% to 11.69% on loans for land development, and from 11.67% to 11.47% on loans for pre-sold single-family construction. The NAHB AD&C survey also revealed that 32% of respondents who built single-family homes during the third quarter of 2026 financed some of their homes with a construction-to-permanent (one-time-close) loan made to the ultimate home buyer. On average, 58% of the homes these respondents built were financed in this manner. While the market for residential mortgages has been showing signs of stress recently—including a recent decline in mortgage applications and increase in delinquencies —it is important not to overlook the role access to AD&C credit plays in helping builders and developers expand the supply of affordable housing. More detail on credit conditions for residential builders and developers is available on NAHB’s AD&C Financing Survey web page . items.title: Nearly Two-Thirds of Phoenix-Area Residents Have Considered Moving Because of Housing Costs, New Survey Finds
items.description:
Nearly Two-Thirds of Phoenix-Area Residents Have Considered
      Moving Because of Housing Costs, New Survey Finds
       New survey finds widespread concern about affordability and support for
         expanding single-family rental housing for Phoenix-area residents

PHOENIX – November 17, 2026 – Nearly two-thirds of Phoenix-area residents have considered moving
because of housing costs, and 91% say housing affordability is a serious problem, according to a new
survey of Phoenix-area residents. Yet most are unaware that Congress recently passed federal
legislation, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, to address affordability concerns.

The survey also found support for expanding access to single-family housing, including newly built rental
homes. Among the key findings:

   ●   Affordability pressures are widespread: Over 91% of Phoenix-area residents say housing
       affordability is a serious problem, and 65% have considered moving because of housing costs.
   ●   Residents want housing choices, including access to single-family homes: 68% believe
       people should have access to single-family homes whether they rent or own, compared to those
       who believe they should only be available to people to own.
   ●   A majority of residents support new rental housing: 55% of Phoenix residents support
       building more rental homes, nearly 2-to-1 over those opposed.
   ●   Renters are feeling affordability pressures: 77% have considered moving because of housing
       costs.


“Housing affordability challenges are affecting communities across the country, and these results
underscore the need for more housing options. No single housing type will solve today’s housing
shortage. We need more opportunities for homeownership, more rental choices, and a continued focus
on expanding supply so families can find housing that meets their needs,” said Adrianne Todman, CEO
of the National Rental Home Council and former Acting Secretary of the U.S. Department of Housing and
Urban Development during the Biden Administration.

The findings come as Arizona policymakers continue to weigh housing affordability, following federal
action this past summer. The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act authorized several new programs,
streamlined existing programs, like the HOME grant program, and placed limits on large institutional
investors from purchasing existing single-family homes.

“As state policymakers look ahead to 2027,” Todman said. “the opportunity is to help families find a home
that works for them, close to the jobs and communities they’ve built their lives around.”

About the survey
The survey of 600 Phoenix-area residents was conducted by Pollfish in September 2026.

items.title: Members Of Congress Have Questions For Brookfield After Its Mass Mobile Home Purchase
items.description: Brookfield quietly closed on the acquisition of the largest privately held manufactured housing portfolio in the United States this year, prompting some members of Congress to inquire about the investment giant’s plans for the properties it now owns. Bisnow/Ethan Rothstein Brookfield purchased Yes Communities from GIC, Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund, in the second quarter, public filings and statements from Brookfield management indicate. Brookfield hasn’t publicized its acquisition of the Denver-based operator of nearly 300 manufactured home developments, but three Democrats from the House of Representatives nonetheless sent a letter to the firm last month voicing concern about the purchase and seeking pledges for tenant protections. Reps. Maxwell Alejandro Frost, Gabe Vasquez and Rashida Tlaib asked management at New York-based Brookfield Asset Management, the publicly traded arm of Toronto-based Brookfield, and Brookfield Real Estate Group to provide assurances that residents’ quality of life wouldn’t be impacted by the deal. The representatives gave BAM until Nov. 20 to respond. The asset management giant hadn’t yet replied as of mid-November, Frost’s office confirmed to Bisnow on Nov. 9. Brookfield didn’t respond to multiple requests for comment. It hasn’t formally announced the acquisition, which was first rumored to be in the works in September 2025, but BAM said in second-quarter filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission that it acquired “the largest privately held U.S. manufactured home portfolio.” Yes Communities operates more than 55,000 housing sites across the U.S., with a focus on the Southwest, Midwest and Southeast. A purchase price for the portfolio is unknown, but BAM said it spent $5.2B in the second quarter on its real estate business, including the manufactured home portfolio and the take-private of an industrial outdoor storage portfolio. Brookfield announced a $1.2B all-cash deal in February to buy Peakstone Realty Trust, a REIT with 60 IOS properties and 16 traditional industrial assets. In its second-quarter filings, Brookfield Real Estate Income Trust disclosed a new investment in a 2% ownership interest in 294 manufactured housing properties at a book value of $86.6M, which aligns with the number of properties under the Yes Communities banner. BAM Chief Financial Officer Hadley Peer Marshall also disclosed on the second-quarter earnings call that a Brookfield fund had made its first investment by deploying capital to Yes Communities. Other affiliates of Brookfield may have also contributed capital for the Yes Communities acquisition. Brookfield REIT said in an investor presentation on its website that as of Sept. 30, it owned a 294-community manufactured housing portfolio across 23 states, the same number of states Yes Communities is active in. Wikimedia Commons; Office of Maxwell Frost Democratic Reps. Rashida Tlaib, Gabriel Vasquez and Maxwell Frost have asked Brookfield about its acquisition of Yes Communities. Executives from Brookfield held one virtual meeting with residents and their advocates following the acquisition that was facilitated by the Private Equity Stakeholder Project and MHAction, two nonprofit advocacy groups, PESP confirmed to Bisnow . GIC and another unnamed institutional investor acquired a 71% equity interest in Yes Communities in 2016, with Stockbridge Capital Group holding on to the remaining stake. Brookfield was reportedly in talks with GIC about acquiring its stake for more than $10B, and it is unclear exactly the size of Brookfield's interest in Yes Communities or how much it paid. In their letter from Oct. 13, the three members of Congress sought details about the acquisition. The letter outlines previous tenants' complaints with Yes Communities for high rent increases, excessive fees and neglect of routine maintenance and says that Brookfield “has the opportunity to change this scenario” and “support meaningful protections for its residents.” “Given the challenges our constituents have experienced at Yes! properties, as well as broader concerns about the private equity business model, we seek assurances that Brookfield will prioritize improving residents’ quality of life and protecting their economic and housing stability, rather than exacerbating the economic challenges they already face,” the representatives wrote. The letter specifically asks Brookfield to disclose whether it plans to increase rents by more than 3% annually, to outline its policy regarding new and existing fees, and to confirm whether it will refrain from serial eviction filings for routine rent collection. The housing legislation that made it to the president’s desk includes new restrictions on existing home purchases from institutional investors but carves out broad exemptions for new development of single-family communities built as rentals. But the March analysis found wide differences across the six cities examined, and corporate landlords own more than 10% of the single-family housing stock that is available for rent in half the cities surveyed. items.description: After four years as senior vice president of development at Swire Properties , Kevin Davenport is joining MaryAnne Gilmartin 's team to lead her Manhattan-based firm's South Florida expansion. Courtesy of MAG Partners Kevin Davenport previously worked at Swire Properties and BGRE, formerly Brookfield Properties. MAG Partners named Davenport the senior vice president and head of development of South Florida, according to a release. The company is also looking to lease office space in Downtown Miami, reported Commercial Observer, which first reported the announcement . "Miami has grown into a global city, with the capital, talent and demand to support large, complex, mixed-use projects," MAG Partners wrote in a LinkedIn post on Thursday . "The projects that will define the region are being built now, and they depend on strong partnerships and teams that know how to deliver at scale. That is the work we do." The new role comes after MAG sought to hire a seasoned development executive to head a mixed-use tower with a hotel, luxury condos and retail spanning more than 1M SF at the beginning of this year. It is unclear where MAG is in the process of the unnamed project. MAG Partners declined to disclose any details about its Miami office lease and the project. Davenport's recent work with Swire included leading the development of the 2.7M SF Residences at Mandarin Oriental , Miami, which broke ground last month . He also led the predevelopment of Swire's planned 1.7M SF One Brickell City Centre office project before it was canceled and the site was sold to The Melo Group last year. Before Swire, Davenport spent 10 years at Brookfield Properties , which rebranded to BGRE in July, and held positions at Hines and the Blackstone Group , according to his LinkedIn. “MaryAnne and the MAG Partners team share my development ethos: a commitment to great design, thoughtful execution and creating places that have a lasting impact,” Davenport said in a statement. “I’m excited to build the company’s presence in South Florida.” This will be MAG Partners' first known venture into South Florida, according to its website. Gilmartin spearheaded the development of the Barclays Center basketball arena while working as an executive with Forest City Ratner before she was named CEO in 2013. After more than two decades with the company, she stepped down from her role and founded MAG Partners in 2018. MAG Partners has designed, built and operated more than 16M SF of office, residential and mixed-use projects with a total value of more than $10B, according to the release. The company has a handful of projects in New York, mainly mixed-income multifamily buildings, according to its website, and is now developing 122 Varick St. in Hudson Square with Global Holdings. New York-based companies have long had a presence in South Florida, but as the region grows in popularity, drawing the ultra-wealthy and their companies , more pros are dividing their time between the Big Apple and the Magic City. items.title: New Firm Seeks Funds For $250M Tysons Project With Conservative Vision
items.description: A fledgling company led by a right-wing political operative is raising money for a half-million-square-foot mixed-use project in Tysons featuring a for-profit conservative institute. But it hasn’t yet picked a site or spoken to local officials about the project. And the scope of the company raises questions about whether it will be able to secure the funds to make it happen. Keyserling Management Group, founded in April, is scouting for sites for a project that is estimated to cost between $200M and $250M, the firm announced in a press release last week. Its vision includes a center “for high culture in innovation and science,” a 165-room hotel, up to 200 apartments, office, retail and restaurant space, a park, a public atrium and a chapel theater. The center, dubbed the Kayden Institute, would be designed for research and development and educational publishing and would offer classes promoting continental philosophy that has been “suppressed in modern times,” according to its website . Keyserling Management Group A conceptual rendering of Keyserling Management Group's envisioned Tysons mixed-use development The mixed-use component is there to help whet investors’ appetites to put funds into both the cultural aspect as well as a more traditional revenue generator with “market acceptable rate of return metrics,” Joseph Michael, CEO and managing member of KMG, told Bisnow in an interview. “It's a way to tie in people, so they would want to do both: not just make money, but also try to help our institutions, our culture, our people, our country,” he said. Michael said he started a private placement offering for accredited investors, focusing on “strategic” partners. KMG has hired SVN Providence Realty Advisors to identify and evaluate sites for the proposed development. The firm has yet to reach out to Fairfax County or Tysons about the project, and at least one Fairfax County supervisor signaled opposition to the ideology behind it when asked by Bisnow . When asked what he would do if the fundraising didn’t come through, Michael said he would self-fund the institute, but likely not with the entire mixed-use development attached. Michael said the hope is to break ground by June 2028. SVN co-founder Terrell Marsh said in a separate interview that he views that timeline as aggressive, and that more realistically, shovels would be in the ground in two to two and a half years. Company’s Founding KMG was founded by Keiko "Kay" Berg in April, who died that same month, Michael said. The company was registered on April 17 with Virginia’s State Corporation Commission and lists an address in the city of Fairfax. KMG’s website lists a different address in Arlington. Underneath the Arlington address, the website misspells its email address as Info@keyerslinggroup.com. Michael told Bisnow that there are more than one but fewer than five employees but did not specify the exact number or disclose any other employees’ names. According to KMG’s website, Berg worked across biomedical device manufacturing, energy and trade industries. The site says that “it was always Kay's intention” for Keyserling to focus on “preserving culture and classical virtues while creating economic success, progress and innovation for future generations three hundred years into the future.” Before April, Michael’s LinkedIn profile says he was a consultant for American Majority Action, a conservative political action group. It says he is an “advocate for America First policies,” campaigned with Fairfax’s GOP committee to elect Virginia Gov. Glenn Youngkin in 2021 and advocated for President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance in the 2024 election. He told Bisnow that he was the campaign manager for Jerry Torres, the Republican congressional candidate for Virginia’s 8th District in 2024, who lost the election. Michael previously worked as a chief operating officer at Centillion Corp. and BUDC Capitol Holdings, according to his LinkedIn profile. Those two companies have little to no internet presence. Michael told Bisnow that those companies no longer have websites. And it would support publishing and master classes on “the magnificent rulers, philosophers, political theorists, and spiritual leaders in history, much of which has been suppressed in modern times.” The website lists about two dozen such figures, largely from Western Europe, including ​St. Thomas Aquinas, Niccolo Machiavelli, Georges Sorel, Friedrich Nietzsche and Thomas Hobbes. items.title: Amid ‘economic headwinds,’ Boston looks to ease its inclusionary zoning policy
items.description: Amid ‘economic headwinds,’ Boston looks to ease its inclusionary zoning policy The city is proposing reduced developer fees and higher thresholds for affordable housing mandates. Published Nov. 16, 2026 Ryan Kushner Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Boston Mayor Michelle Wu on Nov. 10, 2026, proposed a number of changes to the city's inclusionary zoning policy to encourage more development. Getty Images First published on Listen to the article 2 min This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback . Dive Brief: Boston Mayor Michelle Wu last week proposed easing the city’s inclusionary zoning requirements “in the continued face of economic headwinds,” according to a news release. Proposed changes include reducing developer payment-in-lieu fees, extending affordable housing payment schedules and temporarily raising the threshold from seven units to 10 for the size of multifamily housing that must participate. “By providing greater flexibility and reducing upfront costs, we can help make more housing and commercial development financially feasible while preserving the affordability requirements that are so important to Boston’s future,” Boston Chief of Planning Kairos Shen said in a statement. Dive Insight: In a subdued housing market , more cities are adjusting affordable housing mandates for developers. San Francisco this summer slashed its affordable housing requirements for multifamily developers from 15% of units to 5%, according to Mission Local. New Orleans reduced its per-unit affordable housing fee by more than 96% — from $304,810 to $10,000, New Orleans City Business reported last month. Boston’s inclusionary zoning policies, which require 17% of qualifying multifamily units to be income-restricted, have produced nearly 3,000 affordable housing units over the past five years, according to Wu. Wu’s proposal cuts condominium payment-in-lieu fees — fees paid to the city when a developer does not include required affordable units — from 75% to 50% of the difference between market-rate and income-restricted unit values. Developers also could spread out those payments across seven installments instead of two. “This balanced approach is part of our administration’s broader strategy to build more homes, remove barriers to development, and ensure Boston remains a city where residents can afford to stay and thrive,” Wu said. The Boston Planning Department advanced the proposal Nov. 12. Now it will go before the Boston Zoning Commission and the City Council for approval. “We recognize that the cost of building housing has increased, and we want to be responsive to these realities,” Boston Chief of Housing Sheila Dillon said in a news release. “These program changes are designed to encourage the development of new housing while maintaining our commitment to affordability.” Recommended Reading These 3 housing programs are showing results. items.title: Why EAH Housing moved into Oregon to buy 1K affordable units
items.description: Why EAH Housing moved into Oregon to buy 1K affordable units The California-based developer acquired 19 properties from Catholic Charities of Oregon and opened a new affordable community in Sacramento. Published Nov. 13, 2026 Leslie Shaver Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Good Shepherd Village in Happy Valley, Oregon. Permission granted by EAH Housing Properties: 19 Buyer: EAH Housing Seller: Catholic Charities of Oregon Property type: Affordable Units: More than 1,000 Location: Oregon EAH Housing has built a large presence in California and Hawaii with more than 25,000 affordable homes across 240 properties. Earlier this week, the San Rafael, California-based nonprofit owner, manager and developer expanded north by purchasing more than 1,000 affordable homes in the Portland area from Catholic Charities of Oregon, according to a press release. The 19 properties, which include a mix of family, senior and supportive housing communities, are located in the Portland metro area, including Eugene, Sandy and Happy Valley. The acquisition represents the latest in a series of large affordable transitions over the past couple of years. “We view this acquisition as the beginning of a broader presence in Oregon and will continue exploring opportunities to expand our affordable housing portfolio across the state,” Katherine Fleming, EAH’s chief portfolio officer, told Multifamily Dive in emailed comments. “We are focused on identifying mission-aligned opportunities that support the long-term preservation and availability of affordable housing in high-need areas.” Oregon expansion Catholic Charities of Oregon was seeking a mission-aligned nonprofit partner committed to the long-term preservation of affordable housing and approached EAH, according to Fleming. “The acquisition represents a natural extension of the organization’s mission into the Pacific Northwest, where EAH Housing sees significant opportunities to address growing affordable housing needs,” Fleming said. While the acquisition allows EAH to continue preserving affordable housing, Catholic Charities will continue to provide supportive services to residents, according to the release. Guardian Real Estate Services will stay on as manager following the sale. Purchase and sale agreements are now in place for the transaction, which EAH and Catholic Charities have been working on since January 2026, per the release. Financial closings and property transfers are expected to occur on a rolling basis until the second quarter of 2027. Fleming said EAH is “evaluating opportunities for improvement across the properties to ensure they continue to provide high-quality affordable housing for Oregon residents for years to come.” Catholic Charities remains involved CEO of Catholic Charities Kaleen Deatherage said transitioning the properties to EAH Housing allowed them “to remain in the hands of a nonprofit deeply committed to affordable housing.” “Catholic Charities got into affordable housing to serve people,” Deatherage said in the release. “That purpose has not changed. What has changed is our understanding of where we can make the greatest impact.” Catholic Charities was represented by Jackson Ross of Newmark's Affordable Housing Advisors team. In addition to the Oregon acquisition, EAH also opened On Broadway, a new 140-unit affordable mixed-use housing community in Sacramento, according to a Nov. 13 news release shared with Multifamily Dive. The property, which includes one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments across two five-story buildings, serves individuals and families earning between 30% and 60% of the area median income. Thirty-seven homes are permanent supportive housing for individuals and families experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Major affordable deals The EAH Oregon acquisition is only the latest large affordable housing transaction in recent years. In May, nonprofit multifamily affordable housing investment manager National Equity Fund completed a massive deal acquiring National Affordable Housing Trust’s properties and fund management portfolio. In all, NEF is gaining 165 properties, encompassing 15,000 affordable homes nationwide, across 29 funds from NAHT. In December 2025, New York City-headquartered affordable housing preservation company Hudson Valley Property Group acquired a 22-property portfolio comprising 4,768 units across the western United States from Spokane, Washington-based Inland Group. In November 2024, New York City- and Los Angeles-based Standard Communities acquired a 100% affordable housing portfolio of over 6,000 apartment homes in more than 60 communities in four states. With the purchase of the portfolio, valued at over $1 billion, Standard entered Arizona, Colorado and Texas and grew its California portfolio to nearly 11,000 apartments. In May 2023, Chicago-based Nuveen acquired a portfolio of more than 12,000 units concentrated in New York City from New York City-based Omni Holding Co. This portfolio included several large apartment properties in the Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens, as well as buildings in Maryland, Massachusetts, Texas and other states. items.description: Realpage’s New York lawsuit tests the limits of algorithmic rent-pricing bans RealPage Inc. v. James “could provide meaningful guidance on how far state and local governments can go in regulating or restricting these technologies,” a lawyer told Multifamily Dive. Published Nov. 16, 2026 Julie Strupp Senior Editor Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Scott Heins via Getty Images Listen to the article 6 min This audio is auto-generated. A lawsuit regarding New York state’s algorithmic rent-setting ban is testing how far the government can go in restricting such tools without also overly impeding commercial speech, and may provide more clarity about what is within legal bounds, legal experts say. Although it’s difficult to estimate how influential the ultimate decision in RealPage Inc. v. James will be, the preliminary ruling indicates “the case could provide meaningful guidance on how far state and local governments can go in regulating or restricting these technologies without running afoul of the First Amendment,” Corinne Migliazza, associate at real estate law firm Otten Johnson, told Multifamily Dive in emailed comments. In 2024, the Department of Justice and several states sued Realpage and several major landlords that used its pricing product, alleging in United States et al. v. RealPage Inc. et al. that the use of algorithmic software to coordinate rents violated antitrust law. As settlements from that case started rolling out, New York became the first state, in 2025, to impose an outright ban on residential rent-pricing algorithms with its antitrust law amendment S.7882 . Before New York’s ban was set to take effect last year, Realpage went on the offensive. It sued the state in November 2025 on free speech grounds rather than making antitrust arguments. Then it asked the court to halt the ban while its case was being heard. The federal judge agreed to grant a preliminary injunction at the end of September and also denied the state’s January request to dismiss the lawsuit. Judge Valerie Caproni said that some language of the ban likely restricts protected speech more broadly than necessary because it is “undiscerning in targeting software without regard to its use of public versus non-public data.” Although the judge indicated the decision would be a close call, her ruling hints that the court is skeptical of New York’s restrictions, “at least enough to allow more evidence and fact to be developed and presented,” according to Migliazza. “There are also suggestions that the Court may be more receptive to narrowly tailored restrictions, like the initial RealPage settlements, which restricted the algorithms to publicly available information, rather than prohibiting their use outright,” Migliazza said. It remains to be seen whether the court will address particular uses of algorithmic rent-pricing tools in depth. It may decide to only rule on the constitutionality of New York’s restrictions and put the ball in the legislature’s court to find a better solution, according to Migliazza. “Certainly, a First Amendment victory by RealPage would force the legislature back to the drawing board to contour the law towards constitutionality – meaning they would have to make the restrictions less severe,” Migliazza said. New York case impact Algorithmic rent-pricing restrictions are proliferating: New Jersey’s FAIR Act is set to take effect on July 1, 2027, although it is structured differently from New York’s law. Jersey City, New Jersey; Providence, Rhode Island; Philadelphia; Minneapolis; San Francisco; Seattle; Rockville, Maryland, have also passed similar measures. That growing patchwork of algorithmic pricing laws is making compliance more complicated for the rental housing industry, Peter Carstensen, antitrust expert and professor of law emeritus at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, told Multifamily Dive. “What's a developer to do, especially if those regulations are in some way contrary to each other?” Carstensen said. It’s important for rental housing firms to follow these information exchange lawsuits and antitrust litigation more broadly, and to ask, “What are the red lights or the yellow lights that we need to watch out for? How do we make sure that people down in marketing are not creating problems for us?” according to Carstensen. Indeed, landlords are not necessarily in the clear to use algorithmic pricing tools, legal experts at law firm Lowenstein Sandler wrote. They urged caution in New York, and said to prepare for changes in New Jersey and varied algorithmic pricing laws more generally. “Tools that pool competitors’ nonpublic data, discourage price reductions, standardize lease terms, or otherwise limit independent decision-making should be closely reviewed,” according to Lowenstein Sandler. Consultation on the front end to ensure compliance with the relevant jurisdiction’s regulations could save a lot of time, energy and money later on, according to Migliazza, particularly as such regulations continue to evolve. “There is no doubt that as the technological landscape surrounding artificial intelligence changes, the legal one will too,” she said. I've never been able to replicate the feeling that Budapest holds anywhere else," she said. EU citizens can work remotely from Hungary long-term if they meet certain requirements, while Hungary's White Card scheme, which provides one- or two-year residency permits for digital nomads from outside the EU, requires a net monthly income of at least 3,000 euros ($3,370). Coworking space Liftoff in Budapest is located in a former elevator factory, where elevators for the Hungarian Parliament Building were made. Liftoff Coworking There are around 35 co-working spots in central Budapest, according to the Coworking Hungary Association, several of which are in the bustling District VI, near the fashionable bars and restaurants of the Jewish Quarter. Alongside these hubs, the city offers around 35 serviced offices, including locations from larger providers such as Regus and DBH Flex. "Budapest has its own vibe," said Áron Levendel, a founder of co-working space Kaptar, which is within view of the city's striking St Stephen's Basilica. "Whoever wants to connect, make friends or meet people, has an easy job. Whoever wants to have fun, learn or get experiences in English, will have the challenge of choosing from hundreds of options every evening," he said. 'Community' offices Levendel and his co-founders are organizational developers who wanted a workplace that was both sociable and professional. In 2010, they came up with the idea for Kaptar (the word means "hive" in Hungarian). "Gmail was already there, but most of the work was not in the cloud or online yet; people had folders and papers. Digital nomads were not a thing," Levendel told CNBC by email. "Co-working" also wasn't a term in common use at the time, so he called the space a "közösségi iroda," or community office. Since the Covid-19 pandemic, Kaptar has grown more than 30% every year, according to Levendel, including a "wave" of digital nomads who joined after the pandemic, often arriving initially for a month but staying for up to a year. Overseas members either keep an existing job and work remotely, or they are freelancers who can travel, Levendel said. Coworking space Liftoff has an international community from central and eastern Europe as well as the U.S., the United Arab Emirates and Israel. One of Liftoff's team members is also a remote worker who regularly participates in Nomad Cruise voyages, or "workation" trips that combine a conference program with land excursions. Gyurity expects the digital nomad trend to continue, noting that AI now allows individuals to create and launch services or businesses without the resources of a large organization. "More people will be able to imagine their knowledge, skills and opportunities outside the traditional corporate world," she said. At the same time, she recommends that those in the corporate world spend time in a co-working environment. "Most people are there because they are trying to solve something," she said. "Every day I meet younger people who are at a very different stage of their lives and careers, use different tools, and approach problems differently. We can learn from each other." items.title: Blackstone seeks $3B for real estate secondaries fund
items.description: Blackstone is eyeing its next opportunities in the industry amid leadership turnover at the company’s real estate arm. Blackstone is seeking to raise at least $3 billion in a real estate secondaries fund, Bloomberg reported . The secondaries market involves buying and selling existing stakes in private capital funds, often from investors seeking an early exit. Strategic Partners, Blackstone’s in-house secondaries business, raised $2.6 billion for a similar fund back in 2023; Blackstone bought Strategic Partners from Swiss bank Credit Suisse in 2013. Blackstone declined to comment on the fundraising plans. Mining the secondaries market can be appealing to investors seeking exposure to stable and cash-flowing assets. Firms can target specific sectors they believe in, unlike primary commitments, which often involve committing capital to a blind pool of properties. Blackstone is not the only firm playing the secondaries game. Earlier this year, George Walker’s Neuberger Berman raised more than $1 billion for NB Real Estate Secondary Opportunities Fund II LP, exceeding the company’s target for the fund by 30 percent and surpassing the predecessor fund by 48 percent. SIGN UP That fund is set to target interests in mature real estate funds, including from limited partners searching for liquidity. It’s expected to be focused on the middle market and be geared towards the United States and Europe, as well as slight exposure to Asia. In the backdrop of Blackstone’s latest move, however, is the upheaval unfolding in its real estate ranks. Investors are raising questions after Nadeem Meghji and Kathleen McCarthy departed within nine months of each other. The churn comes amid weak fund performance: real estate has been the company’s worst-performing sector for nearly three years. The new co-heads, Giovanni Cutaia and David Levine, are looking to logistics, data centers and hospitality assets as they try to turn the page on a tumultuous period. — Holden Walter-Warner Read more New York Blackstone buys real estate funds in $3B record-breaking deal

items.title: A NorthPark Coffee Crawl
items.description: Live Poll I’m a street walker. You heard right. If there’s a street in an Italian city, I’ll walk it. Verona, for me, is the quintessential Italian walking town. There are two piazzas, Piazza Bra and Piazza delle Erbe, linked by a well-worn pathway—don’t try walking on it in a rainstorm; you will slip and fall—filled with the well-known fashion boutiques of Italy and France. And of course the street is dotted with countless coffee and gelato shops, which are frequented by the locals who stroll about unhurriedly. In the car-forward culture of Dallas, it’s a rare sight. But there is one place I’ve found where I can recreate a little speck of Italy. And for coffee lovers, this is a mecca. In 1965, Raymond Nasher opened an indoor shopping plaza, NorthPark Center, that approaches the Italian retail and coffee experience in spirit. You may not think of NorthPark as a coffee destination, but consider this: the possibilities run from seasonal favorites at Starbucks or Ebar by Nordstrom to places like La La Land Kind Cafe and Caffè Lavazza at Eataly , where the caffeinated concoctions range from deeply traditional ones coming out of Torino to the sun-drenched fantasies of the Left Coast. Guides The Definitive Dallas Coffee Guide Dallas is a city of coffee fanatics, aficionados, and nerds. Find your favorite. By Eve Hill-Agnus | January 12, 2026 | 6:22 pm Many of us got our introduction to coffee culture via Starbucks , and for novices and disciples alike, it’s still the default. But I am painfully introverted, so when I see the lines and all the people, I have the perfect pivot. Fewer than 150 steps away from the East Wing location is a second Starbucks. Find it, sans the line, on the second level just inside Macy’s , where you can score an espresso or a seasonal coffee drink, be it pecan, pumpkin, or peppermint. An introvert’s dream. My other walking town, Torino, is a city tourists often skip on their way through Italy. Pity, for it is to the Piedmont wine region what San Francisco is to Napa and Sonoma. It is also a coffee and chocolate pilgrimage destination, and where I had my first Bicerin—layer upon layer of espresso, hot chocolate and cold cream. Eataly was born in Torino in 2007 and has since expanded all over the world, including to Dallas. Caffè Lavazza at Eataly (first level) is all about the classic specialty coffee drinks that Italians adore. Find your Bicerin there. Caffé Lavazza's marble top espresso bar with its own cappuccino station (aka where the coffee magic is made). Courtesy Eataly Dallas While you’re at the register, notice the sign offering a caffè sospeso. That means you pay for two coffees and drink one, leaving the second “suspended” for whoever comes in and needs it, no questions asked. It’s a Neapolitan practice —an act of kindness handed down by word of mouth, revived after the war, and brought to Dallas when Caffè Lavazza opened in 2021. Getting a coffee at La La Land Kind Cafe is like sitting in the gate line at Burning Man—prepare to chill a bit. There are always hopeful javaphiles and tea devotees queuing for a Banana Cloud Latte or a French Toast Latte, fueled by espresso or matcha, depending on one’s preferred octane. Italy never saw anything like it, but here we are in the age of the oat-milk cloud. I bet you didn’t know there’s a secret spot at NorthPark where lounging guests get a complimentary macchiato. I’d love to tell you, but then it wouldn’t be a secret. (Hint: I have left enough clues for attentive gumshoes to crack the case.) For coffee connoisseurs curious about how to pull a proper ristretto or build a better flat white, a couple of places will teach you the finer points of foam and crema, and sell you a machine to make your own. Between Neiman Marcus and Nordstrom on level one, you’ll find Nespresso and Williams Sonoma . Both carry machines for the home barista, and both offer classes in making the perfect cappuccino. Italians have mastered the aperitivo hour. Why else are outdoor cafés always filled with folks sipping spritzes? For caffeine-crazed souls who want a little more punch in the throttle, there are espresso martinis. They swarm NorthPark, where most every spirit-pouring restaurant has its own version, and the local buzz says Joey Dallas makes one of the best in the city. Who knew espresso martinis were such a pervasive species? If you’re like me and have a sweet tooth, you can chase dinner with an affogato (Italian for “drowned”), espresso poured over a scoop of gelato, typically fior di latte. Eataly’s Terra on the third floor, La Pizza and La Pasta on the second, or the gelato bar by the east entrance will satisfy the urge. You can also pause for an affogato at Paciugo , the gelato stand on the second level where the casual cafés converge. It’s a necessary indulgence, from time to time. They say Europeans outlive us because they walk so much. Italians have the ritual of the passeggiata , a leisurely after-dinner stroll through the town piazza (or, in this case, NorthPark Center, my stand-in for Verona). Thirty years ago, if you’d told me Texas would one day embrace coffee culture the way I saw it in Italy, I wouldn’t have placed a bet. But what I saw in Seattle in those years (drive-through espresso kiosks!) foretold a wave that eventually reached our state. I still get a laugh out of folks sipping hot coffee in the dead of summer, though we’ve stretched our iced-tea habit to coffee, too. Now we can stay cool and caffeinated out of our minds, and we don’t have to hop on a dreaded plane to Italy for the perfect espresso. recent_coverage.title: JLL Arranges $212.5M Sale of Senior Living Community in Lincolnwood, Illinois

recent_coverage.title: Significantly Weaker Demand for Residential Mortgages and CRE Loans in Third Quarter

recent_coverage.title: Just 3 Major U.S. Metros Are Seller’s Markets–the Fewest Since the Pandemic Freeze

recent_coverage.title: Apartment Loans Fuel A Booming CRE CLO Market Not Seen Since 2021
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Bisnow 援引 Trepp 数据称，前 10 个月投资者购买 $40.2B CRE CLO 债务，同比按金额增长 66%；受利率不确定性影响，部分发行人或推迟至明年。

recent_coverage.title: JLL Brokers Sale of 330-Unit Apartment Community in Wildwood, Florida
recent_coverage.summary_zh: JLL 经纪出售佛州 Wildwood 的 330 户 The Juliette，买方为 Centennial Holding；物业建于 2024 年，成交时入住率为 96%，交易价格和贷款金额未披露。

recent_coverage.title: Broe Real Estate Group Acquires 22-Story Apartment Tower in Uptown Dallas
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Broe Real Estate Group 收购达拉斯 Uptown 的 22 层、345 户 Maple Terrace Residences；物业于 2024 年启用，交易价格未披露，JLL 负责经纪。

recent_coverage.title: More Than Half of Raleigh-Area Residents Have Considered Moving Because of Housing Costs, New Survey Finds

recent_coverage.title: Weekley Homes Spends $16M on 38-Acre Dev Site in Scottsdale

recent_coverage.title: ATTOM Reveals July as Best Month to Buy a Home Based on Lowest Premium above AVM
recent_coverage.summary_zh: ATTOM 对过去 10 年逾 48M 笔单户住宅和公寓销售的分析显示，7 月购房溢价最低，为高于市场价值 6.3%；12 月 24 日单日溢价最低，为 3.2%。

recent_coverage.title: GAMLS: Home prices increase despite overall market slowdown
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Georgia MLS 数据显示，亚特兰大 10 月房价中位数同比上涨 1.3% 至 $395,000；成交量同比下降 19.5%，住宅签约量同比下降 26.8%，在售库存上升 1.4%。

recent_coverage.title: Dermody Adds Tracy Warehouse to West Region Industrial Portfolio
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Dermody 收购 Tracy 一处 606,343 平方英尺的 Class A 物流设施，物业建于 2023 年并可即时入住；交易金额未披露，Colliers 将负责招商。

recent_coverage.title: Monthly Mortgage Payments Fall to Lowest Level in 6 Weeks as Home Prices Keep Dipping
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Redfin 称，截至 11 月 8 日的四周，房价中位数同比下降 0.9% 至 $388,613；按 7.18% 利率计算的月度按揭支付降至 $2,755，但住宅签约量仍处记录低位。

recent_coverage.title: First Look: Construction on AT&T’s New Plano Campus Is Underway
recent_coverage.summary_zh: AT&T 已在 Plano 新总部园区铺设首条光纤并举行奠基仪式；公司预计最早于 2028 年底开始迁入员工，园区建成后可容纳 10,000 人。

recent_coverage.title: Weekly Housing Trends: U.S. Market Update (Week Ending Nov. 7, 2026)
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Realtor.com 表示，截至 11 月 7 日的一周，按揭利率连续三周下降但仍处 7% 以上；新挂牌量已连续六周下降，本周出现两位数跌幅，买卖双方参与度均走弱。

recent_coverage.title: The Generational Housing Divide: Millennials Had It Better Than Baby Boomers–Until the Pandemic Changed the Math
recent_coverage.summary_zh: Redfin 称，疫情后按揭利率从约 3% 升至接近 7%，房价同步上涨；疫情后购房的千禧一代住房支出约占收入 35%，许多人因此被排除在市场之外。

recent_coverage.title: AI borrowers now drive nearly half of long-dated U.S. IG issuance. PIMCO sees 3 diversifiers

recent_coverage.title: BWE Arranges $240M Recapitalization of Midwest Seniors Housing Portfolio

recent_coverage.title: Clarion Partners Closes $206M Vegas Industrial Buy

recent_coverage.title: Affinius Capital Provides $100.3M Construction Loan for Student Housing Project Near University of Pittsburgh
